scope: Feasibility of a blocking native ToolRpc call from QuickJS into a real filesystem-capable Golem tool. Not a child_process backend or production performance benchmark.
experimentalBindingOverride: Synchronously lower golem:tool/host@0.1.0#[method]tool-rpc.invoke-and-await; retain the upstream async WIT declaration. Only the generated native wrapper is changed.

measurements.rssScope: Whole native test process, including dependency setup, component analysis, all modes and reconstruction; not per invocation or variant.
measurements.timingScope: End-to-end owner-agent -> JS tool -> optional write-file child -> outer result and output collection. Warmup and initial component analysis are excluded from rows.
caveats: Verbose DEBUG tracing was enabled and another local build was active.
Nested rows include tool discovery, input encoding, admission and the actual filesystem tool body; differences do not isolate the sync import overhead.
The baseline uses node:fs inside the same JS tool, not a separate Node.js distribution.
Rows are evidence for the feasibility fixture, not predicted performance of an implemented child_process backend.

fullWorldSetupObservation.observedStage: Component analysis/compilation; Wizer sampling showed Cranelift register allocation. No nested tool call had begun.
fullWorldSetupObservation.note: The full SDK world also completed Wizer, but its cold compiler cost made it unsuitable for this focused iteration. This does not establish which individual unused interface causes the cost.
